tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a business class.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: How certain industries are reacting to rapid changes in technology
options.B: A relatively recent phenomenon that is affecting businesses
options.C: Challenges faced by the photography industry
options.D: How innovative products and services lead to greater profits for businesses

questions.stem: What is the first stage of the process mentioned in the talk?

options.A: A  company conducts market research to determine what customers want.
options.B: Multiple rounds  of development are performed to perfect a new product.
options.C: A new product or service unlike any on the market is introduced.
options.D: A long-established product or service is recognized as no longer satisfying customer needs.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention digital photography?

options.A: To provide an example of how disruptive innovation affected an industry
options.B: To explain how consumer preference are affected by digital disruption
options.C: To suggest that digital disruption occurs more frequently now than in the past
options.D: To describe the long-term affects of digital disruption on a society

questions.stem: What does the speaker cite as a negative impact of disruptive innovation?

options.A: New products are created that are inferior to existing products.
options.B: Companies that are slow to adapt may struggle to maintain their share of the market.
options.C: Prices for popular products and services may increase suddenly.
options.D: Important sectors in the economy may be overlooked as companies look to innovate.

tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk on a political science podcast.

questions.stem: What aspect of populism is the speaker mainly discussing?

options.A: Its use of rhetoric to affect public opinion
options.B: Its effectiveness as a political strategy over the years
options.C: How it evolved in  the twentieth century
options.D: How it influences modern politics

questions.stem: What point does the speaker make when she mentions left- and right-wing populism?

options.A: There is a sharp contrast between the two wings.
options.B: Left-wing populism has become more popular.
options.C: Both wings focus on connecting with ordinary people.
options.D: Neither wing can provide a satisfactory resolution to political issues.

questions.stem: Why does the speaker mention slogans or catchphrases?

options.A: To suggest that they are effective only in certain political contexts
options.B: To emphasize how complex modern politics can be
options.C: To criticize populists' use of overly simplified language
options.D: To illustrate a communication strategy used by populists

questions.stem: According to the speaker, what is a consequence of populism?

options.A: It increases social tension by promoting conflict.
options.B: It brings opposing political groups closer together.
options.C: It increases public interest in complex policy debates.
options.D: It promotes unrealistic expectations among the public.
